text: One of the problems I have with agentic coding is that I end up with lots of workspaces and branches sticking around long after they're useful. Right now, on my Prelude project landing page, I have a design branch that claims to have an open PR, even though that PR was merged, and I already have an attempted fix that didn't solve the problem. Let's explore some kind of a relatively mechanical (as opposed to agentic) utility that allows me to see which branches/workspaces/sesssions can be cleaned up and then the ability to actually clean them up.

I think I've found why the PR still shows as open, and I have a plan for the cleanup tool. I haven't built anything yet.

## Why the merged PR still says "open"

- **The open-PR label is never cleared.** "Pull request open" comes from a `published` field in `~/.prelude/builds.json`. It's set when the branch is pushed (`server/branches.js:625`), and nothing ever clears it or checks whether the PR was merged.
- **Cleanup only removes a branch whose last commit is in main.** The automatic cleanup (`tidy()` at `server/branches.js:635`) removes a branch only when its last commit is already in main (`:476`). Your branch kept going after #33 merged: this session is working on it now. So its last commit isn't in main, it's never removed, and it still claims the PR is open. A squash-merged PR would hit the same problem, because main gets a new commit rather than the branch's own.

## Proposal: a "Clean up…" window on the project page

It would open from the In progress card and list everything that has piled up. Each item gets a plain reason, worked out by rules rather than by an agent:

| What | How it's detected | Default |
|---|---|---|
| A branch whose work is in main | last commit is in main or origin's main | checked |
| A branch whose PR merged, with work since | the commit that was pushed is in main | unchecked, says "N commits since the merge" |
| A squash-merged branch | the branch's changes are already in main | checked |
| A branch with nothing done | still where it started, older than about a week | checked |
| An entry whose worktree folder is gone | listed in `builds.json` but no folder on disk | checked |
| A stray worktree or `prelude/*` branch | in git or on disk but not in `builds.json` (e.g. an abandoned fix) | unchecked |
| A pushed branch on origin | the remote copy of anything removed | separate checkbox, off by default |
| Folders a previous cleanup couldn't delete | still on disk, usually held by a running program | checked |

- **Never offered for removal:** anything with uncommitted changes, or with a turn running right now.
- **The Remove button** works through the checked items, stopping any running design host first as cleanup does now. Each removal is recorded under "Merged lately", and the page refreshes.
- **Separately, a small fix:** the PR pill would show only while the pushed commit isn't in main, so your branch would stop claiming its PR is open.

A few questions before I build it:

1. **By "sessions", do you mean the agent conversations stored in each design's `sessions/` folder?** Those are merged into main as history. Or do you mean running agents and design hosts?
2. **Should this live on each project's page, or on Home across all projects?** I'd start with the project page.
3. **Should it ever delete branches on origin?** I'd make that opt-in each time.

I've added the cause and this open question to `NOTES.md`.

The "is this commit in main" check misses squash merges completely. A squash merge puts one new commit on main, and none of the branch's own commits are ever part of main's history. So the check stays false forever, and that's one of the ways a branch gets stuck. It needs a check on the content instead.

**1. A trial merge (I'd use this one).** Git can merge the branch into main in memory, without touching any files: `git merge-tree --write-tree main <tip>`. If the result is exactly main's current content, merging the branch would change nothing, so its work is already in main.
- It works for squash, rebase and ordinary merges.
- It still works after main has moved on.
- It's offline and needs no GitHub or Azure tools.
- It needs git 2.38 or newer.

**2. Comparing patches (`git cherry`).** This matches commits by their changes, which handles rebase merges. It misses squash merges, because one squashed commit doesn't match the branch's several smaller ones. I'd skip it.

**3. Asking the Git server.** `gh pr view <branch> --json state` or `az repos pr list --status completed` gives a definite answer: merged, closed or open. It only works when the tool is installed and signed in, so it's a confirmation, not the base check.

**Your case: a branch that kept going after a squash merge.** Running the trial merge on the whole branch would show differences, because of the new work. So Prelude needs to record which commit it pushed; today it only records when and the PR's address. If merging that pushed commit into main changes nothing, the PR's part has landed. Everything after it is "N commits since the merge", and the PR pill goes.

**Where it can still be wrong:**
- **Main later undid or rewrote some of those files.** The trial merge then shows differences, and the branch looks unmerged. That errs towards keeping a branch, which is the safe direction. The server's answer, where it's available, overrides this.
- **The same changes reached main some other way.** The branch looks merged, which is fine: there's nothing in it to lose.
- **The Git server deleted the branch after the merge.** Many are set up to do that, but it's only a hint, never proof on its own.

I've added this to the open question in `NOTES.md`. Should I go ahead with the trial merge, confirmed by `gh`/`az` when they're available, as part of the cleanup window?
Committed to prelude/project-landing-page (2fdb528).
Regarding your previous questions: 1) I kind of meant running agents. But I'm not sure if that's really a problem. 2) Project page for now. 3) Yes, opt in.

1	# Rules: Project Landing Page
2	
3	- **R-v7q.** A project's Needs you lists the same things Home does, for that project alone, newest first, and isn't shown when nothing needs the person there.
4	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
5	- **R-2hx.** A design with a branch is listed under In progress and not under Designs; once its branch is finished, it's listed under Designs again.
6	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
7	- **R-k4n.** Pushing a branch is always asked first, saying which branch goes to which remote, and nothing is pushed until the person says yes.
8	  *shown-on: /f/:project/branches/:branch/publish @ typical*
9	- **R-8dz.** The page's work and its app follow what happens elsewhere without a reload: a turn, a build, a push or a merge changes them as it happens, and they're read again every five minutes for what Prelude can't see, such as a pull request merged on the Git server.
10	- **R-wm3.** New design offers the design system and the app shell as kinds only until the project has one of each.
11	  *shown-on: /f/:project/designs/new @ new-project*
12	- **R-r6b.** A design under Designs says it's ready to build when it has approved pages not yet built, and only once the project's app exists. A design that changed since it was approved isn't ready: it says it changed, until it's approved again.
13	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
14	- **R-h2w.** Once the app is built, it can be run from the project's own folder with a command and address of its own, never the design host's, and the Run button always shows the command it runs, so clicking it is the approval.
15	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
16	- **R-p7c.** Building or connecting the app sets how it runs from here, so a newly built app can be run without setting anything; a command changed on this page applies on this computer only.
17	  *shown-on: /f/:project @ typical*
18	- **R-5tj.** The app run from here opens in the browser once it answers at its address, and stops when Prelude quits.
19	- *

1	# Prelude Design System - notes
2	
3	Prelude's own design system: the vocabulary of Prelude's screens (folders,
4	designs, sessions, the design surface), drafted from what Prelude already ships:
5	`server/public/ds/v1/` (tokens, components, icons) and `server/public/prelude.css`
6	(Prelude's own patterns). Gallery: `screens/01-tokens`, `02-components`,
7	`03-guidelines`; `styles.css` is the gallery's own layout only.
8	
9	## Decisions
10	
11	- **Look unchanged.** Same OKLCH palette (warm neutrals, sienna accent), type
12	  scale, 4px space step, radii and shadows as ds/v1 - it's what Prelude looks like.
13	  Only change: light `--warn` darkened (0.6 → 0.55 L) so warn text reads on white.
14	- **Prelude's own patterns promoted to components**: list/item, menu, segmented
15	  (was `.mode-switch`), toolbar (`.design-bar`), panel (`.chat`/`.design`),
16	  notice (`.host-approval`, confirm cards), status + pulse, transcript, composer,
17	  prose (`.markdown`), empty, crumbs, disclosure, choices. Page layout
18	  (`.page`, `.workspace`, `.bar`) left out: it's the app shell's.
19	- **Compact controls by default.** ds/v1's default button was 3.25rem and primary
20	  4rem (mobile-sized), and Prelude overrode it everywhere with `.small` plus local
21	  heights. Now `.btn` = `--control-md` (2.5rem, same as inputs, so `.inline` lines
22	  up), `.small` = 2rem for toolbars, `.large` = 3.25rem. Primary is a colour, not a size.
23	- **Renames for clarity / one name per thing**: `.f`→`.label`, `.err`→`.error`,
24	  `.sec`→`.secondary`, `.rowbtns`→`.actions`, `.iconbtn`/`.icon-btn`→`.icon-btn`,
25	  `.hard`→`.danger`, `.linkish`→`.link-btn`, `.pill.ok/.bad`→`.good/.danger` (+`.warn`,
26	  `.accent`), `table.data`→`.table`, `.markdown`→`.prose`, `.area`→`.group-label`,
27	  `.span2`→`.wide`, `.kinds .check`→`.choices .choice`. Added `.hint`.
28	- **Layout primitives**: `.stack`, `.cluster`, `.grid`, `.split` (main + `.side`),
29	  `.center` (`.narrow`). Prelude had no general helpe

I've designed the Clean up window, but I haven't rendered it, so check it in the preview. Open it with **Clean up…** at the foot of In progress on the Project page, typical state.

**The window** lists only what Prelude doesn't tidy up by itself, each with its reason. Nothing goes until you click **Remove what's picked**.
- **Picked to start with:** a stray branch whose work is in main, a folder left from an earlier tidy-up, and a branch made a week or more ago and never worked on.
- **Not picked, with a warning:** Underwriting queue, whose pull request was squash-merged with 2 commits since (it lists the 2 files they touch), and a stray worktree with work not in main and 2 files never committed.
- **On origin:** branches on the remote are a separate group under a warning, and none is ever picked to start with.
- **Running agents:** a branch the agent is working in shows as working and can't be picked. Nothing else is done about running agents. No state shows this case yet.
- **Afterwards:** the window closes, the page refreshes, and a notice names what was removed.

**The stale pull request:** Underwriting queue's branch now says "Pull request merged · 2 commits since", with a line offering to push those commits for another pull request or clean the branch up. A branch that is still waiting on its pull request says "Pull request open" as before. Squash merges are detected with the trial merge we discussed, and automatic tidy-up uses the same check, so a squash-merged branch with nothing since goes by itself.

**One gap in the design:** removing Underwriting queue in the preview doesn't take it out of In progress, because the design can't change two lists in one go. The real app would remove it.

**What else changed:**
- **Views brought back:** I copied `page`, `_work` and `_branch` from the app into the design, along with the page's other partials unchanged. The new views are `_cleanup` and `_cleaned`.
- **States:** typical and large project now have things to clean up, so the typical screens you approved will look different.
- **Rules:** added R-t5w, R-c3j, R-9xk and R-m2e, all proposed.
- **Design system:** I added "rows to pick" to the list component, a row whose whole width is a checkbox's label, and noted it in the system's `NOTES.md`.
